extraFacts.fact: 12L14 and 12L15 are leaded free-machining low-carbon steel grades used for turned fittings and plugs; zinc or other plating is added separately.
extraFacts.source: ASTM A108 (cold-finished carbon steel bars, grades 12L14 and 12L15)

extraFacts.fact: Steel hose fittings, plugs and couplings are normally classified under HS subheading 7307.99, brass fittings under 7412.20 and pneumatic push-in fittings of plastic under 3917.40; the importer's customs broker has the final say.

A hose dash size is the hose inside diameter in sixteenths of an inch: -06 is 3/8 inch, -08 is 1/2 inch, -10 is 5/8 inch, -12 is 3/4 inch and -16 is 1 inch. Aeroquip refrigerant hose sizes in this range are quoted with their own inside diameters, as the size table shows.
extraFacts.source: SAE J517 hose size convention; Aeroquip size table on the FJ3019 and FJ3052 listings

faqs.q: What are Adapt-All hydraulic hose plugs used for?
faqs.a: Adapt-All hydraulic hose plugs are carbon-steel plugs, listed in 14 sizes from 8 mm to 48 mm fitting size, that blank off a hose or fitting end. The listing calls the rows hydraulic hose adapters; the pressure figure on each row is the rating for that size.

faqs.q: How do I read an Adapt-All plug part number such as 9029-22X1.5?
faqs.a: 9029 is the Adapt-All series, and 22X1.5 reads like a metric thread: 22 mm fitting size with a 1.5 pitch. Every row follows this, so 9029-08X1.0 is 8 mm, 9029-27X2.0 is 27 mm and 9029-48X2.0 is 48 mm, with the item text confirming the mm size.

faqs.q: Which sizes do the Adapt-All hose plugs come in?
faqs.a: The 14 part numbers run from 9029-08X1.0 (8 mm) to 9029-48X2.0 (48 mm). The pitch changes with size: 1.0 for 8 and 10 mm, 1.5 for 12 to 26 mm and 2.0 for 27, 33, 42 and 48 mm. Send us the thread size on the fitting you need to blank.

faqs.q: How do I pick the Adapt-All plug size for a metric fitting?
faqs.a: Measure the outside diameter and pitch of the male thread on the fitting or the thread of the port, and choose the row with the same mm size and pitch, such as 9029-18X1.5 for an 18 mm x 1.5 thread. The listing does not state the sealing form, so send a photo if the thread is worn.

faqs.q: What pressure can Adapt-All hydraulic hose plugs take?
faqs.a: The size table gives a pressure for each row, and it falls as the size grows: 345 bar for the 8 and 10 mm plugs, 276 bar for 12 to 20 mm, 241 bar for 22 to 26 mm, 207 bar for 27 mm, 172 bar for 33 mm and 138 bar for 42 and 48 mm. Use the figure on the row you order.

faqs.q: What are Adapt-All hydraulic hose plugs made of?
faqs.a: They are carbon steel, in grade 12L14 or 12L15 as the listing states; both are leaded free-machining steels that turn well. The listing gives no plating or stainless option, so for wet or marine service ask us what the maker can supply before you order.

faqs.q: Do Adapt-All hose plugs follow a standard?
faqs.a: The listing names no standard for the plugs, only the material grade and the pressure for each size. If your project needs a specific thread standard or a material certificate, say so in the enquiry and we ask Adapt-All what it can document for the size you need.

faqs.q: What do Adapt-All hydraulic hose plugs fit onto?
faqs.a: They fit a metric male port or fitting with the matching mm size and pitch, for example 9029-24X1.5 for 24 mm. The sealing form is not stated on the listing, so confirm it from the port or a photo; our [dust caps and plugs shelf](/c/dust-caps-plugs) has other ways to close a line.

faqs.q: How should an Adapt-All hose plug be fitted and checked?
faqs.a: Clean the thread and seat, fit the plug and tighten it to the torque for its thread and sealing form, then pressure-test the line before use. Never exceed the row's pressure figure; the [make-up torque guide](/blog/hydraulic-fitting-make-up-torque) explains how far to turn a hydraulic fitting.

faqs.q: Adapt-All hose plugs or dust caps: which one do I need?
faqs.a: A plug closes a live or pressure-tested line and is sized to a pressure, such as 138 to 345 bar on this listing, while a dust cap only keeps dirt out of a fitting. Use a plug where the line may see pressure; see the [dust caps and plugs shelf](/c/dust-caps-plugs) for caps.

faqs.q: Where are Adapt-All hose plugs made, and can they be exported from Dubai?
faqs.a: The listing gives China as the country of origin. We export the Adapt-All hose plugs from Dubai, UAE to the GCC, Africa, Asia and beyond, with the invoice and packing list prepared for your destination. Steel plugs normally fall under HS 7307.99.

faqs.q: Do you keep Adapt-All hydraulic hose plugs in stock in Dubai?
faqs.a: Yes, the Adapt-All hydraulic hose plugs is held in stock at our Dubai, UAE warehouse and ships worldwide with the best lead times. Share the part numbers (for example 9029-12X1.5 or 9029-27X2.0) and quantities on [the contact page](/contact) and we will quote.

faqs.q: What is the Aeroquip FJ3019 male O-ring hose fitting used for?
faqs.a: The Aeroquip FJ3019 is a steel male O-ring hose fitting, listed as a 90° o-ring fitting for use with a short pilot, in 7 part numbers from 0.31" to 0.63" hose inside diameter. The listing names refrigerants including 134A, R12, R22, R404A and R502, so it is a refrigerant-hose fitting.

faqs.q: How do I read an Aeroquip FJ3019 part number such as FJ3019-02-0608S?
faqs.a: FJ3019-02-0608S is the FJ3019 series followed by a variant number, then two size pairs and an S. The last pair gives the hose dash size, as the row text shows (08 dash here), while the first pair differs on some rows, such as 06 with 08. Quote the part number in full.

faqs.q: Which hose sizes does the Aeroquip FJ3019 fitting come in?
faqs.a: The listing has 7 part numbers, FJ3019-03-0606S to FJ3019-07-1010S, for 6, 8, 10 and 12 dash hose, which the row text gives as 0.31", 0.41", 0.5" and 0.63" inside diameter. Check the hose inside diameter against that column before you order.

faqs.q: How do I choose the right FJ3019 part number for my refrigerant hose?
faqs.a: Match the hose dash size and inside diameter in the row text, then the other size pair to the port; FJ3019-02-0608S is the row for 8 dash hose. Quote the hose type and size with the part number so we can check the fitting, ferrule and crimp setting against the hose.

faqs.q: What pressure is the Aeroquip FJ3019 fitting rated for?
faqs.a: The maker states 500 psi (34 bar) for the FJ3019 range, and every row of the table carries 34 bar. That is the fitting's stated figure; an assembly is rated by the hose and fitting together, so send the hose and working pressure for confirmation.

faqs.q: Which refrigerants and materials suit the Aeroquip FJ3019 fitting?
faqs.a: The fitting is steel and the listing names refrigerant types 134A, MP39, MP66, R12, R22, R404A and R502. Compatibility also depends on the hose liner, so tell us the refrigerant and oil before ordering the FJ3019.

faqs.q: Does the Aeroquip FJ3019 fitting follow a standard?
faqs.a: The listing names no standard for the FJ3019, only its pressure, size range, material and the refrigerant types. If your project needs a specific standard or certificate, say so in the enquiry and we ask Eaton Aeroquip what can be supplied.

faqs.q: What does the Aeroquip FJ3019 male O-ring fitting connect to?
faqs.a: It is a male O-ring end, so it connects to a female O-ring port or nut of the matching size; the listing does not state the thread, so send the mating part or a photo. It must be crimped onto the hose series it is designed for.

faqs.q: How is the Aeroquip FJ3019 fitting assembled onto refrigerant hose?
faqs.a: A crimp fitting is rated only on the hose series it is designed for, so quote the hose type and size with the FJ3019 part number. We then check the fitting, ferrule and crimp specification against the hose before supply; see our [hydraulic hose assembly guide](/blog/hydraulic-hose-assembly-guide) for the sequence.

faqs.q: How does the Aeroquip FJ3019 differ from the FJ3052 straight fitting?
faqs.a: The FJ3019 is the 90° version while the FJ3052 straight fitting is the other body style, with the same 500 psi (34 bar) stated rating and size range. See the [Aeroquip FJ3052 straight fitting listing](/p/aeroquip-fj3052-series-male-o-ring-hose-fittings) for its rows.

faqs.q: What is in the Aeroquip hydraulic hose fittings listing?
faqs.a: It is a mixed listing of 14 Aeroquip hose fittings: crimp and screw-together ends, 45° and 90° elbows, NPTF and JIC ends, in brass and steel, listed for the GH493 hose series. Pick the row by its part number and its item text, as the rows are not one style.

faqs.q: How do I read part numbers such as 1BA20FJA20 and 06906E-104 on the Aeroquip listing?
faqs.a: The part numbers follow several Aeroquip schemes, so they do not share one decode: 1BA20FJA20 and 1BA16FJB16 end in a size, 06906E-104 reads as a style then a size, and 4741-6B and 4741-12B are barbed JIC ends. Quote the number in full and we confirm it.

faqs.q: Which hose sizes do the Aeroquip hydraulic hose fittings cover?
faqs.a: The 14 rows run from 3/16" (06904E-102) to 1-1/2" (1AA24FJB24), with 1/4", 5/16", 3/8", 1" and 7/8" between, and dash sizes -8 and -16 in the item text. Send the hose inside diameter and the end you need and we pick the row.

faqs.q: How do I choose between 45° and 90° rows in the Aeroquip fitting listing?
faqs.a: Take the row whose item text names your angle: 1BA20FJA20 is the 45° fitting at 1-1/4" and 1BA16FJB16 is the 90° elbow at -16 hose dash. The spec field says 45° elbow for the listing, but the rows include other shapes, so confirm the angle with us.

faqs.q: What pressure are the Aeroquip hydraulic hose fittings rated for?
faqs.a: The listing gives no pressure rating, and the table carries no pressure column for these rows. A crimp fitting is rated only on the hose series it is designed for, so send us the hose, its working pressure and the part number and we confirm the combination.

faqs.q: What are the Aeroquip hydraulic hose fittings made of?
faqs.a: The material field reads brass x brass, brass, steel and steel, so the rows are a mix of brass and steel, and the finish is trivalent chromium zinc. Check the item text of your row for the metal, and tell us the fluid if brass could be a problem.

faqs.q: Which hose series are the Aeroquip hydraulic hose fittings for?
faqs.a: The listing gives the GH493 series, and says a crimp fitting is rated only on the hose series it is designed for. It does not name a fitting standard; quote the hose type and size with the part number and we check the fitting, ferrule and crimp specification before supply.

faqs.q: What end connections do the Aeroquip hydraulic hose fittings have?
faqs.a: The type field reads crimp, female JIC swivel with a 37° thread angle, and rows include NPTF x hose ends, JIC x hose barb and 3/8-18 NPT. Match the end to the port: a JIC swivel needs a male 37° flare, an NPTF end a pipe port; see our [JIC adapters](/c/jic-adapters).

faqs.q: How are Aeroquip hose fittings assembled onto hose?
faqs.a: Crimp fittings go on with the crimp setting for the hose series, and the 'screw together' row (38-190627-16-16) is a reusable style that is assembled by hand. Quote the hose type and size and we confirm which method applies; see our [hydraulic hose assembly guide](/blog/hydraulic-hose-assembly-guide).

faqs.q: Aeroquip hydraulic hose fittings or Parker crimp fittings: how do I choose?
faqs.a: Choose by the hose: a crimp fitting is rated only on the hose series it is designed for, so an Aeroquip fitting goes with Aeroquip-series hose, and a Parker fitting with Parker hose. For Parker 26 and 43 Series fittings see the [braided hose crimp fittings shelf](/c/braided-hose-crimp-fittings).

faqs.q: What are Legris 90 degree nylon push-to-connect elbows used for?
faqs.a: Legris 90 degree elbows are black nylon push-to-connect elbows for compressed-air tubing, in 38 part numbers for metric and inch tube and several male thread ends. They join a tube to a tube, or a tube to a threaded port, at a right angle where a tube cannot bend.

faqs.q: How do I read a Legris elbow part number such as 3109 62 22?
faqs.a: The four-digit family tells the second end: 3102 is push-to-connect by push-to-connect, 3109 is push-to-connect by male NPT or BSPT, 3182 is push-to-connect by tube stem and 3199 is push-to-connect by male metric or BSPP. Then two pairs give tube and thread size, so 3109 62 22 is 1/2 inch tube by 1/2 inch NPT.

faqs.q: Which tube and thread sizes do the Legris 90 degree elbows come in?
faqs.a: The 38 rows cover tube from 3/16" and 4 mm up to 1/2" and 14 mm, for example 3102 04 00 (4 mm), 3102 12 00 (12 mm), 3182 62 00 (1/2"), with male ends from 1/16" to 1/2" NPT, BSPT, BSPP and metric. Choose the row by tube size and the thread on the port.

faqs.q: How do I pick the right Legris elbow for my air line?
faqs.a: Choose the end type first, then the tube size: 3102 joins two tubes, 3109 screws into an NPT or BSPT port, 3199 into a BSPP or metric port. Match the tube outside diameter, such as 6 mm or 1/4", to the row's item text, and note that most rows are packs of 10.

faqs.q: What pressure and temperature can Legris nylon elbows take?
faqs.a: The maker states 260 to 290 psi (18 to 20 bar) depending on size, with most rows at 20 bar, a temperature of 176°F and vacuum to 28 in. Hg. Use the figure on your row, and do not use them above the stated temperature.

faqs.q: What are Legris 90 degree elbows made of, and what media suit them?
faqs.a: The elbows are black nylon, listed as chemical resistant and corrosion resistant, for air. The listing gives no list of other fluids, so for water, oil or any gas other than air, tell us the medium before you order.

faqs.q: Do Legris push-to-connect elbows follow a standard?
faqs.a: The listing names no standard for the elbows, only the pressure, temperature and vacuum rating. The thread forms on the male ends are NPT, BSPT, BSPP and metric, so match the port thread; ask us if you need a material declaration for a project.

faqs.q: What do Legris 90 degree elbows connect to?
faqs.a: The push-to-connect end takes semi-rigid nylon, polyurethane or similar tube of the stated outside diameter, and the other end screws into a port or joins a second tube. For other push-in styles see our [push-to-connect pneumatic fittings shelf](/c/push-to-connect-pneumatic-fittings).

faqs.q: How do I fit and release a Legris push-to-connect elbow?
faqs.a: Cut the tube square, push it fully into the elbow until it stops, and pull gently to check it is held; to release, press the button ring and pull the tube out. Use a thread sealant on tapered NPT or BSPT ends.

faqs.q: Legris nylon elbows or Dixon push-in elbows: what is the difference?
faqs.a: Both are push-in elbows, but the Legris listing is all nylon in 38 part numbers with male and tube ends, while the [Dixon push-in female elbow](/p/dixon-nylon-nickel-plated-brass-push-in-female-elbows) has a nickel-plated brass female thread and a nylon body. Pick by the port thread.

faqs.q: Where are Legris elbows made, and can they be exported from Dubai?
faqs.a: The listing gives France as the country of origin. We export the Legris elbows from Dubai, UAE to the GCC, Africa, Asia and beyond, with the invoice and packing list prepared for your destination; plastic push-in fittings normally fall under HS 3917.40.

faqs.q: Do you keep Legris 90 degree elbows in stock in Dubai?
faqs.a: Yes. Our warehouse in Dubai, UAE keeps the Legris 90 degree elbows in stock, and we ship worldwide with the best lead times. Put the part numbers (for example 3102 06 00 or 3109 62 18) and the number of packs in an enquiry on [the contact page](/contact).

faqs.q: What are Mi-T-M 90 degree elbows used for?
faqs.a: The Mi-T-M 90 degree elbows are three brass and steel pipe and barb elbows listed as compatible with Mi-T-M equipment: 23-0391 (3/4 inch female, cast brass), 23-0074 (3/8 inch male by 3/8 inch barb, brass) and 24-0096 (1 inch FNPT, black pipe).

faqs.q: How do I read Mi-T-M part numbers such as 23-0391 and 24-0096?
faqs.a: The listing gives no decode for these two-part numbers, so treat them as catalogue numbers: 23-0391 is the cast brass 3/4 inch female elbow, 23-0074 the 3/8 inch male by barb elbow and 24-0096 the 1 inch FNPT black pipe elbow. Quote the number in full.

faqs.q: Which sizes do the Mi-T-M 90 degree elbows come in?
faqs.a: There are three part numbers: 3/4 x 3/4 inch female (23-0391), 3/8 inch male with a 3/8 inch hose barb (23-0074) and 1 x 1 inch FNPT (24-0096). Each is a single size, so check the one you need against these three rows.

faqs.q: How do I choose between the three Mi-T-M elbows?
faqs.a: Choose by the connection you need: a barb for clamped hose (23-0074), a female thread for a male pipe nipple (23-0391 at 3/4 inch) or a 1 inch FNPT black pipe elbow (24-0096). The three are different parts, so confirm the part number against the Mi-T-M machine.

faqs.q: What pressure are the Mi-T-M 90 degree elbows rated for?
faqs.a: The listing gives no pressure rating for the three Mi-T-M elbows, and the rows carry none. Tell us the fluid, working pressure and the Mi-T-M equipment, and we confirm the elbow before you order.

faqs.q: What are the Mi-T-M elbows made of?
faqs.a: The material field reads brass and steel: 23-0391 is cast brass, 23-0074 is brass and 24-0096 is a black pipe (steel) elbow. Brass and black pipe suit different media, so tell us the fluid before ordering.

faqs.q: Do the Mi-T-M 90 degree elbows follow a standard?
faqs.a: The listing names no standard; the FNPT thread on 24-0096 is a US pipe thread and the other rows give only size. Ask us if you need a specific thread standard or a material certificate, and we ask the maker what it can supply.

faqs.q: What do the Mi-T-M elbows connect to?
faqs.a: 23-0391 takes a male 3/4 inch pipe thread, 23-0074 connects a 3/8 inch hose by its barb to a 3/8 inch male thread, and 24-0096 takes a male 1 inch NPT nipple. See our [brass hose barbs shelf](/c/brass-hose-barbs) for other barbed ends.

faqs.q: How should a Mi-T-M brass elbow be fitted?
faqs.a: Clean the threads, apply a thread sealant to tapered pipe threads, and tighten without over-torquing brass, which cracks. On the 3/8 inch barb, push the hose fully on and secure it with a hose clamp.

faqs.q: Mi-T-M elbows or a brass hose barb elbow: which do I use?
faqs.a: The Mi-T-M 23-0074 is a 3/8 inch male by barb elbow made for Mi-T-M equipment. For other barb sizes and thread ends see our [brass hose barb × NPTF male 90° elbow](/p/brass-hose-barb-x-nptf-male-90-elbow), which lists many sizes.

faqs.q: Where are Mi-T-M elbows made, and can they be exported from Dubai?
faqs.a: The listing gives the United States as the country of origin. We export the Mi-T-M elbows from Dubai, UAE to the GCC, Africa, Asia and beyond, with the invoice and packing list prepared for your destination; brass elbows normally fall under HS 7412.20.

faqs.q: Do you keep Mi-T-M 90 degree elbows in stock in Dubai?
faqs.a: Yes. We keep the Mi-T-M 90 degree elbows in stock at our warehouse in Dubai, UAE, and ship worldwide with the best lead times. Send the part numbers (23-0391, 23-0074 or 24-0096) and quantities through [our contact page](/contact) for a quotation.
